user.title: Connect GeoDrops to Google BigQuery
user.description: Paste your Google Cloud service-account JSON key and enter your GCP project id. The service account needs the BigQuery Job User role on your own project. New to this? See the integration documentation (linked below) for a step-by-step setup guide.

data_description.project_id: Your own Google Cloud project, where the queries run and are billed. Not GeoDrops' project.
data_description.credentials_json: The full contents of the JSON key file you downloaded for the service account.

add_device.title: Add a GeoDrops probe
add_device.description: Enter the serial number shown in the GeoDrops app (for example AAA111) and a friendly name.

data_description.serial: The probe's serial number as shown in the GeoDrops app. It must have reported in the last 12 hours.
data_description.name: The name of the probe's device in Home Assistant.
data_description.area_id: The area to put the new device in. You can change it later on the device page.

reauth_confirm.title: Update the GeoDrops service-account key
reauth_confirm.description: Google is no longer accepting the stored service-account key for project {project_id} (it was probably deleted, revoked, or its service account was disabled). Create a new JSON key for the service account and paste its full contents below. Your probes and settings are kept.

data_description.credentials_json: The full contents of the new JSON key file.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure GeoDrops
reconfigure.description: Change the GCP project the queries run and bill in, or paste a new service-account JSON key to rotate it. Your probes and settings are kept.

data_description.project_id: Your own Google Cloud project, where the queries run and are billed. Not GeoDrops' project.
data_description.credentials_json: Leave blank to keep the current key.

error.invalid_credentials: The service-account JSON could not be parsed.
error.cannot_connect: Could not query BigQuery. Check the project id and that the service account has BigQuery Job User.
error.device_not_found: No readings found for that serial in the last 7 days. Check the serial.
error.invalid_auth: Google rejected this service-account key. It may have been deleted or revoked, or its service account disabled. Create a new JSON key and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This GeoDrops project is already configured.

add_device.title: Add a GeoDrops probe
add_device.description: Enter the serial from the GeoDrops app (for example AAA111) and a friendly name.

data_description.serial: The probe's serial number as shown in the GeoDrops app. It must have reported in the last 12 hours.
data_description.name: The name of the probe's device in Home Assistant.
data_description.area_id: The area to put the new device in. You can change it later on the device page.

data_description.scan_interval_minutes: How often to query BigQuery for new readings. Default 20, minimum 5.
data_description.lookback_hours: How far back to search for each probe's latest reading on every poll. Default 12, 1 to 168.
data_description.staleness_warn_hours: Log a warning once a probe's data is older than this many hours. Default 12, at most "Mark unavailable after".
data_description.staleness_skip_hours: Mark a probe's sensors unavailable once its latest reading is older than this many hours. Default 12, 1 to 168.
data_description.expire_after_minutes: Also mark sensors unavailable if a probe's data has not come back from a poll within this many minutes. Must be longer than the poll interval. Default 80.
data_description.offline_alert_hours: Show a repair once a probe's latest reading is older than this many hours, or one repair for the whole integration when every probe is. Default 24, 1 to 168.

error.device_not_found: No readings found for that serial within the lookback window (Advanced options).
error.invalid_auth: Google rejected the stored service-account key. Update it via the integration's Reconfigure option, then try again.
error.invalid_credentials: The stored service-account JSON could not be parsed. Paste a new key via the integration's Reconfigure option, then try again.
error.warn_above_skip: Must not be more than "Mark unavailable after".
error.expire_below_interval: Must be longer than the poll interval, or sensors go unavailable between polls.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.no_devices: There are no probes to remove.

auth_failed.message: Google rejected the stored service-account key: {error}

invalid_credentials.message: The stored service-account key could not be parsed: {error}

access_denied.title: GeoDrops can't query BigQuery
access_denied.description:
Google denied the service account access to BigQuery in project {project_id}. Check that the BigQuery API is enabled on the project and that the service account has the BigQuery Job User role. GeoDrops keeps retrying, and this message goes away once a query succeeds.

Google's error: {error}

max_moisture_required.title: {name} needs its max-moisture calibration
max_moisture_required.description: GeoDrops needs the max-moisture (deep water) test run on probe {name} ({serial}). Until it is, the probe's moisture sensors stay unknown. Open the GeoDrops app, select the probe and follow its "Learn Max Moisture" steps. This message goes away once GeoDrops has the calibration, which can take a few hours to show up.

max_moisture_recalibration.title: {name}'s max-moisture calibration has expired
max_moisture_recalibration.description: GeoDrops asks for the max-moisture (deep water) test to be run again on probe {name} ({serial}). It does this 75 days after the last one. Moisture keeps reporting meanwhile, but its quality drops. Open the GeoDrops app, select the probe and run the deep water test again. This message goes away once GeoDrops has the new calibration, which can take a few hours to show up.

probe_offline.title: {name} has stopped reporting
probe_offline.description: Probe {name} ({serial}) hasn't sent GeoDrops a reading for more than {hours} hours. Check in the GeoDrops app that it is online; a weak Wi-Fi signal or a flat battery are the usual causes. This message goes away on its own once the probe reports again.

data_delayed.title: GeoDrops data is delayed
data_delayed.description: None of your probes has a reading newer than {hours} hours. When every probe stops at once, the delay is usually on GeoDrops' side rather than at the probes. If it lasts, check the GeoDrops app and contact GeoDrops. This message goes away on its own once readings arrive again.
